concept.name: Hinted Handoff, Read Repair & Anti-Entropy

relationships.description: Connects Hinted Handoff & Repair to caching in the broader engineering catalog.

concept.tagline: Three complementary reconciliation layers in Dynamo-style stores: temporary coordinator hints, on-read digest repair, and background Merkle-tree anti-entropy.
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of Dynamo-style repair—from why hints preserve write availability without counting toward quorum to preventing zombie data resurrection via gc_grace_seconds.

spark.summary: Hinted handoff buffers writes on healthy coordinator nodes when a target replica is temporarily unreachable, while read repair and anti-entropy Merkle-tree repair reconcile silent divergence over time.
spark.keyTakeaway: Hinted handoff preserves write availability during brief outages (minutes to a few hours), not durability guarantees; you still need read repair and scheduled anti-entropy repair to prevent zombie data and silent entropy.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** In leaderless Dynamo-style stores (Cassandra, ScyllaDB, Riak), nodes restart, pause in GC, or drop packets daily. Three mechanisms heal replica divergence: 1.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts RF=3 Quorum Write with Hinted Handoff for Downed Replica R3 (Coordinator (W=2 OK) -> Replica R1 (Live) -> Replica R2 (Live) -> Replica R3 (Down)); Anti-Entropy Merkle Tree Pinpointing Divergent Token Sub-Ranges (Root Hash != Match -> Left Hash == Match -> Right Hash != Match -> Key 742).

learningJourney.title: What are Hinted Handoff, Read Repair & Anti-Entropy
learningJourney.explanation:
In leaderless Dynamo-style stores (Cassandra, ScyllaDB, Riak), nodes restart, pause in GC, or drop packets daily. Three mechanisms heal replica divergence:

1. **Hinted Handoff**: When a replica is down during a write, the coordinator buffers `(target_host_id, mutation, timestamp)` locally and replays it once Gossip marks the peer alive.
2. **Read Repair**: On a read, the coordinator compares data/digest responses across replicas and writes the newest timestamp back to stale peers.
3. **Anti-Entropy Repair**: Scheduled background jobs exchange **Merkle trees** (hash trees over token ranges) to find and stream divergent keys—even cold keys never read.

learningJourney.title: Why Hinted Handoff Alone Cannot Prevent Zombie Data
learningJourney.explanation: In Cassandra/Dynamo, deletes write **tombstones** that are purged after `gc_grace_seconds` (default 10 days). If a downed replica missed a tombstone and stayed offline past `max_hint_window_in_ms` (3 hours), and you never ran Merkle anti-entropy repair before `gc_grace_seconds` elapsed, the old value **resurrects as zombie data** when the node rejoins!

ideas.title: Hint Replay Storms
ideas.description: When a node rejoins after 2 hours, dozens of coordinators replaying gigabytes of hints simultaneously can saturate its compaction and network—always configure `hinted_handoff_throttle_in_kb`.

ideas.title: Sub-Range Incremental Repair
ideas.description: Coarse full-ring Merkle trees over-stream entire token ranges on a 1-key mismatch; use vnodes or sub-range repair (e.g., Cassandra Reaper) to isolate differences.

learningJourney.title: Where Leaderless Repair Applies (and Where Consensus Differs)
learningJourney.explanation: Hinted handoff is built for tunable-consistency AP stores; linearizable Raft/Paxos systems do not buffer hints for minority nodes.

benefits: Survives rolling kernel patches and brief cross-AZ blips with zero client errors at p99 = 6.2 ms.
costs: Requires scheduled anti-entropy repair within `gc_grace_seconds` and hint disk/throttle limits.

benefits: Raft/Paxos logs replay committed entries deterministically via `nextIndex` when followers reconnect.
costs: Buffering unacknowledged minority hints on non-owning nodes would violate consensus invariants.

benefits: Stop storing hints past `max_hint_window_in_ms` and rely on anti-entropy streaming when the node returns.
costs: Unbounded hints exhaust coordinator NVMe disk and cause replay storms.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: Coordinator Hint Buffering, Throttling & Tombstone Windows
learningJourney.explanation: Keep `max_hint_window_in_ms` bounded (1–3h), throttle hint replay bandwidth, and schedule incremental repair strictly faster than `gc_grace_seconds` (e.g., every 3–5 days for a 10-day grace period).
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```yaml
# cassandra.yaml production hinted handoff & repair guardrails
hinted_handoff_enabled: true
max_hint_window_in_ms: 10800000        # 3 hours max; stop buffering if peer is dead longer
hinted_handoff_throttle_in_kb: 1024    # Prevent replay storm when node rejoins
max_hints_delivery_threads: 2
hints_flush_period_in_ms: 10000
# Pair with: nodetool repair --incremental every 3-5 days (< gc_grace_seconds = 864000s / 10d)
```
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Comparing the Three Repair Mechanisms
learningJourney.explanation: Each repair layer covers a different failure window and key temperature.

benefits: Lowest-latency catch-up for transient restarts without scanning SSTables.
Reconciles actively read keys immediately before returning to the client.
costs: Adds digest RPCs to all replicas, increasing read tail latency on mismatches.

benefits: Guarantees eventual consistency for cold, never-read keys and purges tombstones safely.
costs: Full SSTable validation scans consume CPU and compaction/streaming I/O.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Production Anti-Entropy: Merkle Tree Exchange Over Vnode Ranges
learningJourney.explanation: When two replicas exchange 32-level **Merkle trees** for a vnode token range, matching root hashes prove 100% equality in `O(1)` network bytes. Only the mismatched leaf sub-ranges are streamed.
